decisions.reason: Links the top-level import in client.js to the classic-script combo in the boot log and the compile error in browser-error.txt. Explains that one parse failure stops every entry from registering and that typert-registry is only the first awaited entry.

Bisects the insert rows and describes the ModuleLoader.load id/factory shell with package-name id, React through the injected require, and inject/apply exports. But its main static check is node --check (plus grep), which can accept ESM, rather than a real classic-script parse.

Correctly says another entry owns the declaration and kind/scope do not belong to the registrant. But it treats register as a declaration and replaces it with an invented inject(slotName, Component) call. It never explains the ordering problem or wraps register inside inject to defer it.

Uses the boot log and restart notes: the combo is built once at boot, so the fix is a full host restart, taskkill /T /F for the orphaned tree, then refresh and check the plugin list. Explains EADDRINUSE as the old process still holding the port.

Host side proposes per-bundle classic-script parsing and attributing the failure to the owning plugin. The checklist covers the loader factory, host React, inject/apply and restart/Windows tree kill, but its slot item repeats the wrong non-deferred inject form.

caps.reason: Does not keep bare ESM, keeps slots.inject instead of immediate registration, forbids kind/scope on the registrant, and requires a host restart rather than a refresh.
